The closed proposal retains void in the List override after the runtime incompatibility was reported. The declared callback type is G[Unit], but already-compiled old clients may still supply other payloads.
The corresponding Vector override also retains conversion; repairing only the generic default misses this dispatch path. This is experimental PR source, not evidence that narrowing shipped.
The exact PR-head runner calls the old-compiled consumer method. Its MimaExceptionsTest name must not be confused with static MiMa signature analysis.

claims.rule: For erased generic API changes, test an old-compiled caller against the new runtime and inspect every specialized override, not only MiMa signatures or the default implementation.
claims.applicability: Closed PR 4352 establishes the G[String]-to-G[Unit] runtime-cast hazard. Existing Cats build separates old compile dependencies from current Test runtime; verify current baselines before running.
claims.counterexample: Recompiling every client against the narrowed signature cannot reproduce old-bytecode compatibility. Conversely, source-incompatible changes may be intentional in an approved breaking release.

claims.rule: For a new cached instance in an inherited public Scala 2 trait, consider a concrete def delegating to a private cached value and verify generated compatibility rather than adding a new val field.
claims.applicability: PR 3392 corrected an incorrect assumption about Scala 2.12 trait compatibility. This is a targeted historical strategy, not proof that every def addition is compatible or every val must be changed.
claims.counterexample: Replacing an already-published val arbitrarily can itself affect compatibility; a private non-inherited object value is not the problematic public trait addition.
